matchup_findings.statement: Louisville's rushing offense meets a North Carolina defense it out-rates on the matchup scale (+2.33) (rush success rate, opponent-adjusted: Louisville offense #17 of 138, North Carolina defense #123 of 138).
Louisville holds the early-down edge: its offense stays ahead of the chains on 1st and 2nd down against this defense (+2.44) more than North Carolina does (+0.89).

Louisville owns the stronger opponent-adjusted explosive-play matchup: North Carolina offense vs Louisville defense -0.76, Louisville offense vs North Carolina defense +1.18 (explosive-play rate, opponent-adjusted: Louisville offense #1 of 138, North Carolina defense #10 of 138).

Louisville's passing offense meets a North Carolina defense it out-rates on the matchup scale (+1.36) (pass success rate, opponent-adjusted: Louisville offense #17 of 138, North Carolina defense #76 of 138).

Louisville owns the stronger opponent-adjusted sustained-efficiency matchup: North Carolina offense vs Louisville defense +0.68, Louisville offense vs North Carolina defense +1.84 (success rate, opponent-adjusted: Louisville offense #14 of 138, North Carolina defense #102 of 138).
Louisville's sustained-efficiency edge is real but not decisive (1.17, below the 2.0 strong threshold): enough for the trailing side to stay in range.

pace.definition: possession_environment = (z of home offense plays + z of away defense plays allowed + z of away offense plays + z of home defense plays allowed) / 2, on adjusted values. volatility.definition: offense_ypp_residual_sd = game-to-game spread of the offense's yards per play around what the fit expected against each opponent; its percentile is within the FBS universe. explosive_yard_share_z is the raw share standardised across FBS (not opponent-adjusted). takeaways_per_game_z and giveaways_per_game_z are RAW per-game turnover counts standardised across FBS: turnovers are regression-prone and are deliberately not opponent-adjusted.
